page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What BOD stands for
lines: BOD stands for Biochemical Oxygen Demand.
It is an index used to measure the pollution
load of sewage and of a water body.
steps.why: The expansion of the letters is a mark on its own, so it is written first and in full. The book expands BOD as 'Biological Oxygen Demand'; NCERT and standard usage write 'Biochemical Oxygen Demand', and both forms are seen in papers, so the biochemical form is the safer one to write.
common_mistakes: Writing Biological Oxygen Deficiency. The last word is Demand.
Giving only the letters. The expansion carries the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Three words for three letters: Biochemical, Oxygen, Demand.
steps.margin_note: One line for the expansion, one for what it is used for.

steps.label: What it measures

lines.text: BOD = oxygen needed to break down the waste

lines: BOD is the amount of dissolved oxygen needed
by aerobic organisms to break down the
organic matter in a given water sample, at a
stated temperature and over a stated time.
A high BOD means heavy organic pollution.
steps.why: BOD is an indirect measure — it counts the oxygen the microbes will USE, not the pollution itself — so the sentence must say oxygen needed and must name the organic matter being broken down.
common_mistakes: Writing that BOD is the oxygen present in the water. It is the oxygen NEEDED.
Leaving out the last line. The link between high BOD and heavy pollution is the useful part.
steps.memory_tip: More waste means more microbes, more microbes means more oxygen demanded. High BOD, dirty water.
steps.margin_note: The definition in one long sentence, then the one line that reads the number.

insider_note: The last line is the one an examiner looks for: a high BOD means the water is heavily polluted.
